basics.name: Pranav Chaturvedi
basics.label: Penetration Tester | VAPT Engineer
basics.summary: Cybersecurity & Digital Forensics graduate (B.Tech, VIT Bhopal, 2026) specializing in offensive security — web application penetration testing, exploit development, and vulnerability assessment. Builds custom offensive tooling in Python and runs a self-hosted, segmented pentest range for hands-on practice. EC-Council CEH in progress; currently preparing for OSCP.

work.name: CSI Cyber Secured India
highlights: Identified and assessed security vulnerabilities across client systems and web applications in a structured cybersecurity internship program
Performed vulnerability scanning, security audits, and documented findings using industry-standard tools and methodologies
Gained hands-on exposure to real-world security assessment workflows, reporting standards, and remediation recommendations

work.name: Unified Mentor
highlights: Applied foundational penetration testing and network security concepts to practical assignments and case studies
Contributed to vulnerability assessment projects under mentorship guidance, strengthening professional documentation and threat-analysis practices

projects.name: WebGuardian — Web Vulnerability Scanner
highlights: Python framework orchestrating security tools (nmap, wafw00f, curl, dnsrecon, theHarvester, nikto) via a declarative YAML check registry into 11 automated checks: port/TLS scanning (Heartbleed, POODLE, CCS injection), WAF detection, header disclosure, DNS zone transfer, and web misconfiguration

Concurrent execution via a thread pool and list-based subprocess calls (no shell-injection surface); an 18-test pytest suite covers severity classification and report generation independent of whether the external tools are installed

projects.name: Isolated Offensive Pentest Range
highlights: Built and maintain a network-segmented pentest lab (NAT-enabled and fully isolated libvirt networks) with a headless Kali attack box and GPU-assisted password cracking
Practice against deliberately vulnerable targets: OWASP Juice Shop, DVWA, and Metasploitable2

projects.name: PortSwigger Web Security Academy — SQL Injection Exploitation
highlights: Solved and documented 9 SQL injection labs — including UNION-based, error-based, and blind SQL injection — using self-written Python exploit scripts and Burp Suite proxy analysis
For each lab: authored a self-written Python script automating the exploit end-to-end, plus a technical write-up covering the underlying query logic, discovery methodology, and working payload

projects.name: Intrusion Detection System Using Machine Learning
highlights: Trained and compared 5 classifiers (Random Forest, Linear SVM, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression) on KDD Cup 1999, using a stratified split and per-class precision/recall given severe class imbalance across 4 attack categories

Found that every model, including 99.97%-accurate Random Forest, is worst specifically at detecting User-to-Root (privilege escalation) — the rarest, most severe category, which overall accuracy alone would have hidden

projects.name: Zero-Trust Self-Hosted Infra
highlights: Production-style Nextcloud/MariaDB/Redis stack on Docker Compose with zero exposed inbound ports — admin access via Tailscale, public HTTPS via Cloudflare Tunnel, version-pinned images, an isolated DB container, and automated volume-level backups
